Each limit is given twice: the 95\,\% (upper) or 5\,\% (lower) percentile of the resamples, as the corrected test was planned, and the normal approximation $\hat L\pm1.645\,\mathrm{sd}$ from the variance of the resamples; the two differ where the resampling distribution has heavy tails. TOST $p$: the larger of the two one-sided normal-approximation $p$ values. Fieller: the 90\,\% interval of $R$ from the variances and covariance of the resamples; its upper end is the one-sided 95\,\% upper limit of $R$. Injected odds ratio: the effect on all ground nearest a water-related name whose mean gain reaches the upper limit, range over the four no-effect references (estimator scale in brackets). (a) 4,000 resamples; (b), (c) and the pigeonhole row 500 resamples with the second stage refitted; (d) adds the Nadeau--Bengio variance over 13 fold assignments to (c), so only the normal approximation is defined.
